routes.name: Bellagio, Las Vegas Strip -> Fremont Street Experience
routes.note: The single most-ridden 4 miles in the state. Las Vegas Blvd is a six-lane arterial with no bike facility; the question is what the router offers instead.

routes.name: UNLV -> Downtown Summerlin
routes.note: Straight across the valley grid, 12 miles. Tests whether RTC's bike-lane registry actually reaches the arterials the grid is made of.

routes.name: Las Vegas City Hall -> Water Street District, Henderson
routes.note: The valley's main diagonal. Corridor 4 in corridors.json; audited here for shape rather than existence.

routes.name: North Las Vegas City Hall -> Harry Reid International Airport
routes.note: North-south across the whole urban core past two freeway interchanges. Airports are the classic one-way-area trap; read the failure line before calling anything a defect.

routes.name: Downtown Las Vegas -> Clark County Wetlands Park
routes.note: The valley's flagship off-street ride, along the Las Vegas Wash. Should find shared-use path; if it does not, the RTC path layer is not reaching the graph.

routes.name: Summerlin South -> Red Rock Canyon scenic drive entrance
routes.note: The road ride every Las Vegas cyclist does. NV 159 with a wide shoulder; a 6-mile trip that leaves the urban grid.

routes.name: Water Street District, Henderson -> Boulder City
routes.note: The River Mountains Loop Trail corridor. A 35-mile paved loop exists here; the direct road is US 93/95 freeway. What the router picks is the whole question.

routes.name: Boulder City -> Hoover Dam
routes.note: Corridor 3. Bikes are barred from the bypass bridge; the legal ways are the old dam road and the Historic Railroad Trail through five tunnels.

routes.name: Reno -> Victorian Square, Sparks
routes.note: Corridor 2, and the shortest trip in this audit. The Tahoe-Pyramid Trail runs the whole way along the Truckee; a seam in it is exactly what a 4-mile hop is meant to expose.

routes.name: Reno -> Nevada State Capitol, Carson City
routes.note: Corridor 1. Washoe Valley squeezes everything between two ranges; I-580 is the only continuous line and the rideable answer is Old US 395 / Eastlake Blvd.

routes.name: Carson City -> Spooner Summit, Lake Tahoe
routes.note: US 50 climbing 2,200 ft to the Tahoe rim in 12 miles. A mountain grade with no alternative, and the first real test of the DEM.

routes.name: Incline Village -> Stateline, Lake Tahoe east shore
routes.note: NV 28 and US 50 down the east shore, 22 miles. Nevada's most scenic road ride, partly paralleled by the new Tahoe East Shore Trail.

routes.name: Carson City -> Minden
routes.note: Carson Valley, 15 miles, US 395 with a frontage-road alternative. A flat rural control against the mountain trips above.

routes.name: Elko -> Spring Creek
routes.note: Corridor 6. The only routine bicycle trip in Nevada's northeast, where the network is state highways plus subdivision streets and NDOT's inventories stop.

routes.name: Winnemucca -> Golconda
routes.note: 14 miles beside I-80 on old US 40 / Golconda Rd. Tests whether the frontage road is in the graph or the router is pushed onto the Interstate.

routes.name: Ely -> McGill
routes.note: 12 miles on US 93 in the emptiest quarter of the state. One road, 6,000 ft elevation, and almost nothing else in the graph.

routes.name: Mesquite -> Bunkerville
routes.note: 5 miles across the Virgin River. One bridge, on I-15's frontage system; a severed crossing here is a 40-mile detour.

routes.name: Las Vegas -> Pahrump
routes.note: Corridor 5, and long inter-city trip 1. 50 miles over the 5,500 ft Mountain Springs pass on NV 160, with no parallel road for forty of them.

routes.name: Reno -> Fallon
routes.note: Long inter-city trip 2. 60 miles east across the Truckee Meadows and the Lahontan Valley on US 50 Alt, paralleling I-80 for the first half.

routes.name: Ely -> Baker, Great Basin National Park
routes.note: Long inter-city trip 3, and the loneliest road in the audit: 65 miles on US 6/50 over two 7,000 ft summits with one junction the whole way.
